intro: A door that will not lock, close, or latch properly is a security risk as well as a daily inconvenience. FixWell Services repairs and replaces locks and doors across Salisbury and Wiltshire, from a stiff Yale nightlatch to a failed multipoint mechanism on a UPVC door. We are fully insured, available for same-day emergency callouts, and familiar with the lock types found in Salisbury's varied housing stock. Lock and door repair sits within our broader carpentry services for door, hinge, and frame work. Call +44 7391 599 078 for urgent security repairs or use the quote form.

sections.heading: Lock and Door Types in Salisbury Properties
sections.body: Salisbury's housing stock spans several centuries and building traditions, which means we encounter a wide range of lock and door types in a single working day. Victorian and Edwardian terraces in St Ann Street, Milford Road, and around the Friary typically have solid timber doors with five-lever mortice deadlocks (ideally BS3621-rated for insurance compliance) and Yale-style rim nightlatches. UPVC doors fitted to 1980s–2000s properties across Bemerton Heath, Bishopdown, and Harnham use multipoint locking systems driven by a central gearbox mechanism. Composite front doors on newer Salisbury developments use similar multipoint mechanisms but with a different cylinder type. Understanding which system is fitted is the first step to diagnosing a fault correctly: a door that is hard to lock may have a failing gearbox, a misaligned keep, or simply a dropped hinge that has shifted the door out of alignment with the frame.

sections.heading: Common Lock and Door Faults
sections.body: Cylinder wear is the most gradual fault: the internal cam mechanism wears so that the key turns stiffly, requires jiggling, or fails to engage the lock body. Euro cylinders (used on UPVC and composite doors) are also vulnerable to snapped key extraction and to cylinder snap attacks, which is why BS Kitemark TS007 3-star rated cylinders are now the recommended replacement. Misaligned strike plates cause the latch tongue to scrape rather than seat cleanly in the keep, creating a door that bounces back when pushed shut. This is particularly common in older timber-framed Salisbury homes where the frame has settled over decades. On UPVC doors, a failed multipoint gearbox (the mechanism inside the door edge driven by the handle) is typically identifiable by a handle that turns freely without engaging the locking rods, or by rods that no longer fully extend to the keeps at top and bottom of the frame.

sections.heading: How FixWell Repairs Locks and Doors
sections.body: Diagnosis always precedes repair. We check whether the fault is in the lock mechanism itself or in the door and frame geometry; a door that will not close properly is often a hinge problem rather than a lock problem. For cylinder replacements we remove the existing cylinder using the internal screw, measure the exact dimensions (internal and external backset lengths, total length), and fit a like-for-like or upgraded replacement. For multipoint mechanism failures we disassemble the door edge, identify whether the gearbox, a specific rod, or a keeps alignment is at fault, and supply a replacement gearbox matched to the door brand where possible. Strike plate adjustments involve removing the keep, enlarging or repositioning the recess in the frame with a sharp chisel, and refitting with longer screws to anchor deep into the timber frame. All security repairs are tested through multiple lock-and-unlock cycles before we leave.

sections.heading: Security Standards, Cost, and Salisbury Context
sections.body: For insurance compliance, most UK home insurers require external doors to be fitted with a five-lever mortice deadlock to BS3621 standard and a door chain or viewer on the front door. Where we replace a cylinder, we recommend and fit TS007 3-star rated euro cylinders as standard; these are anti-snap, anti-drill, and anti-pick, providing a meaningful upgrade over standard cylinders at modest cost. For landlords with Salisbury rental properties, a functioning lock on every external door is a legal requirement under the implied covenant of quiet enjoyment and the Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018. Our standard rate is £20–£40/hr with most lock repairs completed in 30–90 minutes; cylinder and mechanism parts are billed at cost. Same-day emergency response is available across Salisbury, Amesbury, Tidworth, and surrounding areas.

sections.heading: Locks, Door Hinges, and the Full Home Repairs Service
sections.body: Lock and door repairs are closely related to door hinge repair; in many cases a door that appears to have a lock fault is actually suffering from dropped or loose hinges that have moved the door out of alignment with the lock keep. FixWell's home repairs service covers both, and a single visit can address hinge tightening, door plane adjustment, and lock mechanism repair together. Where a door has been damaged by forced entry and requires a full replacement, we can advise on the most appropriate option for the property type and coordinate supply. For urgent security failures, including broken locks after break-in attempts, doors that cannot be secured overnight, or snapped keys in cylinders, contact FixWell Services on +44 7391 599 078 for same-day attendance. Use the quote form for non-emergency bookings.

faqs.q: Can you replace a broken lock on the same day in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Yes. For security emergencies (a broken cylinder, a door that cannot be secured, or a snapped key in a lock) we offer same-day callouts across Salisbury and Wiltshire. Call +44 7391 599 078 directly for the fastest response.

faqs.q: My UPVC door handle turns but the door does not lock. What is wrong?
faqs.a: This is almost always a failed multipoint gearbox, the central mechanism that drives the locking rods when you lift the handle. The gearbox wears out over time and is a straightforward replacement. We source a matching gearbox and fit it in one visit.

faqs.q: What does BS3621 mean and do I need it?
faqs.a: BS3621 is the British Standard for thief-resistant mortice deadlocks. Most UK home insurers require all external doors to have a BS3621-compliant lock as a condition of your policy. If you are unsure whether your current lock meets this standard, we can inspect and advise.

faqs.q: Can you remove a key that has snapped inside a lock?
faqs.a: Yes. Key extraction is a standard part of our lock repair service. Depending on the cylinder type, we use extraction picks or remove the cylinder entirely to retrieve the broken key, then assess whether the cylinder needs replacing.

faqs.q: My front door is hard to close and the latch keeps missing the keep. Can you fix it?
faqs.a: Yes. This is usually caused by a dropped hinge moving the door down, or by the door frame settling over time. We identify whether the issue is the hinge, the door, or the keep alignment and carry out the correct adjustment, often a combination of hinge tightening and strike plate repositioning.

faqs.q: Are you insured for lock and door repairs in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Yes. FixWell Services holds full public liability insurance for all lock and door repair work. We are not a locksmith company but carry out the same practical repairs for all common lock types found in Salisbury properties.
